# Per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers a per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web console, giving cluster administrators visibility into workbenches that are sitting idle. For each workbench in a project the report shows its last activity, owner, and reserved resources (volumes and compute reservations), sourced from the notebook controller's existing activity tracking. No changes are made to the notebook controller itself — it already tracks last-activity timestamps; this epic surfaces that data to administrators. This is the read-only reporting foundation administrators asked for; reclamation itself remains a manual, out-of-scope decision.

## Scope

- New report view in the RHOAI web console listing idle workbenches per data science project.
- Report columns per workbench: last activity, owner, and reserved resources.
- Data sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking (the component continues to work unchanged — this is a passive data source).
- Report respects OpenShift project-scoped RBAC so administrators see reports for the projects they administer.
- CSV export of the idle-workbench report with the same columns shown in the console (administrators can export either report as CSV).
- Definition of the idle threshold used to classify a workbench as idle, as an implementation decision made by the dashboard team.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches, when an administrator opens the idle-workbench report, then the report lists each workbench with its last activity, owner, and reserved resources.
- Report values for last activity match the notebook controller's activity tracking for the corresponding workbenches (validation of the passive data source).
- The report is accessible only to users with administrative access to the relevant projects, consistent with the console's existing project-scoped RBAC.
- An administrator can export the idle-workbench report as a CSV file whose columns match the on-screen report.
- The dashboard build pipeline is green with these changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking.
- HLR-3 (P2, partial): Administrators can export either report as CSV — this epic covers CSV export of the idle-workbench report.

# Stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers a stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web console, showing completed pipeline runs older than a configurable age that still retain their artifacts. Old pipeline runs accumulate storage; this report lets cluster administrators see, per project, which completed runs are stale so they can reclaim capacity with confidence. Data is sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines' existing run-completion metadata — the pipelines component continues to work unchanged as a passive data source. Reclamation/deletion of runs is explicitly out of scope.

## Scope

- New report view in the RHOAI web console listing stale pipeline runs per data science project.
- Report columns identifying each stale run, its completion age, and its retained artifacts.
- Data sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata via the platform's existing pipelines interfaces.
- Configurable age threshold that determines when a completed run is considered stale.
- Report respects OpenShift project-scoped RBAC so administrators see reports for the projects they administer.
- CSV export of the stale pipeline-run report with the same columns shown in the console (administrators can export either report as CSV).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing completed pipeline runs, when an administrator opens the stale pipeline-run report, then the report lists completed runs older than the configured age together with their retained artifacts.
- The age threshold is configurable and changing it changes which runs appear in the report.
- Report values match Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata for the corresponding runs (validation of the passive data source).
- The report is accessible only to users with administrative access to the relevant projects, consistent with the console's existing project-scoped RBAC.
- An administrator can export the stale pipeline-run report as a CSV file whose columns match the on-screen report.
- The dashboard build pipeline is green with these changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- HLR-3 (P2, partial): Administrators can export either report as CSV — this epic covers CSV export of the stale pipeline-run report.

# Documentation for idle/stale resource reports and safe reclamation

## Description

This epic delivers administrator documentation for the new idle-resource reporting capability in the RHOAI web console: what the idle-workbench report and the stale pipeline-run report show, where the data comes from, how to use CSV export, and — critically — the safe steps an administrator should follow before reclaiming capacity identified by these reports. Documentation is authored only after both reports are implemented, so it describes what was actually built.

## Scope

Content outline (topics to be authored in the RHOAI documentation set):

- Overview of idle-resource reporting: the problem it solves (idle workbenches holding volumes/reservations, stale pipeline runs accumulating storage) and what is and is not covered (reporting only; no automated reclamation, no cost/chargeback).
- Using the idle-workbench report: interpreting last activity, owner, and reserved resources columns; how idle is determined.
- Using the stale pipeline-run report: interpreting run age and retained artifacts; configuring the stale-age threshold.
- Exporting either report as CSV.
- Safe reclamation steps: the precautions an administrator should take before deleting or scaling down resources identified as idle or stale (e.g., confirming with the workbench owner, verifying artifacts are no longer needed), with explicit warnings about what the platform does not do automatically.
- Accuracy validation of every documented claim against the implemented behavior in the web console.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation explains both reports (idle-workbench and stale pipeline-run), their columns, their data sources, and the configurable stale-age threshold.
- Published documentation explains CSV export of both reports.
- Published documentation includes safe reclamation steps with appropriate cautions, consistent with the strategy's out-of-scope boundary (no automated reclamation).
- All documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reports and verified accurate (screenshots, column names, and configuration steps match the shipped behavior).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps.
